Nature of the Case : Seeking  Compensation/Award Date of commencement of : 20.07.2023 Recording of evidence Date of Judgment : 09.05.2025 pronounced  JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed the petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% p.a. for the damages caused to its Bus.
02.

The facts in brief of the petitioner's case is that, on 18.08.2017 at about 5.50 a.m. when the driver of the petitioner corporation was driving his BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-2220 slowly and carefully by following traffic rules and regulations in the schedule route from Koramangala TTMC to Hebbal and when he reached outer ring road, Kadubisnahalli, near New Horizon College, at that time, one lorry bearing Regn.No. TN-72-AW-1407 which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations, came from back side and dashed to the back side of the bus.
Due to the accident, petitioner's bus has got damaged.
The petitioner has incurred expenses of Rs.1,00,000/- including labour and material charges and sustained loss due to damages to the bus and could not fly on road.

The accident was taken place only due to sole rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing Reg.
No.TN-72-AW-1407 belonged to the 1st respondent and the same is insured with 2nd respondent.
Hence, both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the damages to the petitioner.
03. Respondent No.1 remained absent inspite of service of summons hence he was placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

Bangalore Metropolitan Transport ... vs Mallikarjuna.K on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136674852/
2 04.

In the written statement the respondent No.2 has stated that the petition is false, frivolous,
vexatious and not maintainable at law or on the facts of the case and the same is liable to be dismissed.
The entire petition averments is denied by this respondent.
It is further stated that the petitioner has not suffered any loss as stated in the petition.
It is further stated that, the accident was occurred entirely due to negligent driving of the Bus by the driver of the petitioner corporation who was liable for the accident.

Further, the respondent No.1 is duty bound under Section 134(c) of Motor Vehicle Act to inform the accident and submit all vehicle documents, including the driving license and the Insurance particulars to seek indemnification and this respondent failed and neglected to perform the statutory obligation to seek indemnification.
Further, the owner of the vehicle has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
This respondent has limited liability as per policy of insurance certificate.
The petitioner has suppressed all true and material facts of the accident.
It is further submitted that the driver of the lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-72-AW-1407 drove his vehicle in a slow manner.
The police have not informed the insurer about the alleged accident as required under Section 158(6) of the IMV Act.
Thus there is a violation of the rules and regulations of the M.V. Act.
Among other grounds, the respondent No.2 prayed for dismissal of the petition.

05. Based on the above pleadings my predecessor in office has framed following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, on 18.08.2017 at about 5.50 a.m. when the driver of the petitioner corporation was driving the BMTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-57- F-2220 and when he reached outer ring road, Kadubisnahalli, near New Horizon College, at that time, one lorry bearing Regn.No. TN-72- AW-1407 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the back side of the bus and due to which the bus got damaged?
2. Whether the petitioner further proves that he had spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards labour and material charges?
3. What order or Award?
06.
In order to prove the case, petitioner got examined its Depot Manager in Depot No.14 as P.W-1 and examined one witness as P.W.2 and produced 19 documents, which were marked as Ex.P1 to 19.
The respondent neither lead evidence nor produced documents.
07. Heard arguments on both the sides.
The averments made in the affidavit filed by him is in consonance with the petition averments.
The petitioner deposed that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing No.TN-72-AW-1407 driven by its driver.

In order to substantiate his oral evidence, petitioner has produced the copy of FIS and FIR which were marked as Ex.P12 and P13.
11.

Firstly, in connection with ownership of the vehicle bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2220 is concerned, in the evidence of PW1-Prasanth G.M and PW2-Shivanna P.S. stated that, the petitioner BMTC is the owner of the vehicle in question.
PW.1 is working as Depo Manager of Depo No.14 and Pw2 is working as driver of the said vehicle.

On 18.08.2017., when he was on duty of the BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2220, met with an accident, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Lorry bearing registration No.TN-72-AW-8302.
Consequently, bus was damaged.
In support of the said affidavit evidence, the PW1 on behalf of the petitioner placed, Ex.P.12 to Ex.P.17 for consideration.
The said documents are police documents.

On going through the said documents, it reflect that, on the basis of first information given by PW-1, on the same day of the accident criminal law set in motion against the driver of Lorry bearing registration No.TN-72-AW-8302. alleging that,
he had committed the offence punishable under Sec.279 of IPC.

After due investigation process,
final report has been submitted against the driver of the said vehicle by name Rajesh S. and also the said person has pleaded guilty of the said offence as per Ex.P18 before the Jurisdiction Magistrate.
The said document and also the recitals of spot mahazar, spot sketch and complaint, it is crystal clear that, in the accident in question, vehicle belonged to the petitioner was damaged.
The said vehicle was defending vehicle in the said accident and also driver of the Lorry admits his negligent act and pleads guilty of the offence.
12. Secondly, it is the assertion of the petitioner through the evidence of PW1 that, due to the accident, rare right side of the body was damaged, rare right side portion of door bumper damage.
Due to the said damages, bus in question was unable to complete the schedule trip on the said day and the corporation was suffered monetary loss.

13. In support of the said stand of the PW-1 placed his authorization letter, first information report,
accident report, trip sheet, job card, IMV report, B-register extract, In and out register, Form No.38 marked as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 for consideration.

In the recitals of the Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.11, there is a clear narration about the vehicle number and name of the driver deputed as on the date of the Bangalore Metropolitan Transport ... vs Mallikarjuna.K on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136674852/
4 accident and the route also been noted in the said documents.
As per the Ex.P.17, the bus was damaged to its rear right side of the body, rear right side assembly, rear right side portion of rear bumber.
But there is no document to show the actual loss, no other supportive documentary evidence is available on record.

14. Over all appreciation of the evidence of the PW-1 and 2 along with the documentary evidence,
there is no dispute that, due to the accident, vehicle of the petitioner corporation was damaged and also there is no dispute with respect to the ownership of the vehicle in question.
Further, on going through the Ex.P.19 driving licence, it is evident that, at the time of accident, the driver of the vehicle belonged to the petitioner had valid and effective driving license.

At the time of cross-examination of PW-2, he stated that, he being the driver of the bus belonged to the petitioner, as on the date of accident, was proceeding along with workers of the company, at that time offending vehicle came and caused the accident and he gave complaint to the police.
In this regard, both the vehicles were seized and the vehicle pertaining to the petitioner was taken to the interim custody, after the accident.
And denied the suggestion of other side that, due to his sole negligence, accident in question had taken place and false complaint has been given against the driver of the offending vehicle.
But, no important points culled out from the mouth of this witness to show that, the vehicle of the petitioner was not damaged in the accident.
15. In support of the defences forthcoming in the written statement of the respondent No.2, has not examined any of the person and not marked any document on their behalf.
Hence, I am of the view that, in support of the above issue, the petitioner corporation has placed satisfactory evidence for consideration.

16. It is relevant to note that, for compensation filed U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident, only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required, as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in, 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

entities.text: 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, It was observed that, "When the accident, from the driver of the offending vehicle is proved,
clearly indicates that, due to the said mistake on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, the defending vehicle was damaged."

17. In the light of my due discussions held above, I am of the view that, the evidence of the PW1 and 2 and also the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner substantiate the case of the petitioner.

Hence, I am of the opinion that, petitioner has proved its case that, the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle Lorry bearing No. TN-72-AW-1407.

In the said accident, the defending vehicle BMTC bus, bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2220,
belonged to the petitioner was damaged.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

18. Issue No.2 : The petitioner being the owner of the Bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2220 has contended that, after the accident, vehicle in question belonged to the petitioner sustained damages to its back side, due to which petitioner has suffered a loss of Rs.1,00,000/- .

In order to prove the Bangalore Metropolitan Transport ... vs Mallikarjuna.K on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136674852/
5 same, PW1 who is the Depot Manager in respondent Corporation in depot No.14 has produced Accident First Information report, Accident report form, Job card retail invoice, Letter dt.19.07.2023, RC, B-register extract, Form No.38, In and out register which were marked as Ex.P2 to Ex.P17 which are corroborating with the damages mentioned in the F.I.S, and damages mentioned in IMV report marked as Ex.P17.
Ex.P17 reveals the damages sustained by the bus in the accident.
Hence there is corroboration on comparison of First Information and IMV report.
In the evidence PW.1 deposed that the bus has sustained damages to its right rear side and the right side corner and rear glass is fully damaged.
The repair has been done in their garage itself and the bus was there in the garage for a period of 3 months.
Glass, indicator and damaged body of the bus was repaired.
In this regard, the petitioner corporation has produced job card which reflects that the petitioner has incurred Rs.21,823/- for repairing the bus.
It is further contended that due to the accident bus could not ply on the road for more than 3 months.
Further deposed that, due to accident, bus was unable to give service for three months causing monetary loss to their corporation.
In support of the evidence of this witness not produced any document for consideration.

19. Along with the evidence of PW-1 and PW2, on going through the material documents, reveal that, in the trip sheets there is a clear mention about plying of the defending vehicle in question, as on the date of the accident.

But, there is no supportive documentary evidence is available on record,
in proof of the how much amount has been lost by the petitioner.
20. On the other hand, Ex.P.11, disclose about in and out registers and work charts.
These documents will not support the stand of the PW1 and PW2 to the effect that, due to the damages of the bus the petitioner corporation incurred a monetary loss.

21. At the time of cross-examination of PW-1, answers given by the PW1 reveals that, on the same date of sending the vehicle for repair, the bus in question was out from the workshop and admitted that, the corporation has not placed any documents to show the monetary loss bills for having paid the expenses of the purchasing of spare parts of the bus and also not produced trip cancelled document.

22. Over all appreciation of the documents and the evidence given by the PW1 and PW2, I am of the view that, the petitioner corporation has not placed satisfactory and convincing documents to show that, a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- loss of was caused to the corporation.

Hence, by considering the documents, placed by the petitioner corporation, along with the damages noted in the report of the motor vehicle inspector marked at Ex.P.17, I am of the view that, it is apt to award compensation of Rs.21,823/- towards damages of the vehicle.
The same will meet the ends of justice.

23. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, keeping in mind about the damages mentioned in the recitals of the IMV report, and also inconvenience caused to the petitioner, due to the said damage, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.21,823/-
(Rupees Twenty one Thousand Eight hundred Twenty three only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.

Bangalore Metropolitan Transport ... vs Mallikarjuna.K on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136674852/
6 24.
In the present case the 2nd respondent has admitted with regard to the insurance policy issued by the company in respect of the offended vehicle in favour of respondent No.1.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify the insured.
In view of the above the respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answered this issue partly in the affirmative.

25. Issue No.3:- In view of the above discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.21,823/-(Rupees Twenty one Thousand Eight hundred Twenty three only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount with accrued interest shall be released to the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the open court dated this the 9th day of May 2025)
